subject: Pathology
summary: Abdominal girth is a bedside measure of abdominal distension, reflecting fluid, mass, or organomegaly. It guides urgent assessment and monitoring of abdominal pathology. Clinicians use it to detect ascites, bowel obstruction, or abdominal tumors.

sections.p: Abdominal girth is the circumference of the abdomen measured at the level of the umbilicus or the widest point. It is recorded in centimeters and compared to age‑, sex‑, and height‑adjusted norms.
b: Normal ranges vary by population; typical adult values 70–90 cm

sections.p: Severity is graded by deviation from normal: mild (≤10 cm above normal), moderate (10–20 cm), severe (>20 cm). Staging aligns with underlying pathology: ascites (grade I–III), bowel obstruction (partial/complete), or mass effect.
Common causes in low‑resource settings include:
b: Ascites from liver disease or TB peritonitis
Bowel obstruction from adhesions, volvulus, or intestinal parasites

sections.p: Patients may report fullness, early satiety, abdominal pain, or visible distension. Physical exam reveals a tense or fluid‑filled abdomen, shifting dullness, or palpable masses.
Investigations confirm the cause and guide management.
Urgent signs requiring immediate care include
b: Rapid increase in girth, abdominal pain, vomiting, tachycardia, hypotension, altered mental status

sections.p: Treat the underlying cause first, then supportive care.
b: Ascites: diuretics (spironolactone, furosemide), paracentesis if tense
Bowel obstruction: nasogastric decompression, fluid resuscitation, surgical referral
Masses: oncologic workup, chemotherapy or surgery as indicated
Heart failure: diuretics, ACE inhibitors, beta‑blockers

sections.p: Monitor girth daily, repeat imaging if changes, and manage risk factors.
b: Control chronic liver disease, treat TB, prevent parasitic infections

Certain conditions may mask true girth changes.
b: Severe dehydration can reduce girth despite ascites

t.a: What is the normal abdominal girth for a 30‑year‑old woman?
t.b: Approximately 70–80 cm, but varies with height and ethnicity.

t.a: Can abdominal girth be used to diagnose cancer?
t.b: It suggests a mass but requires imaging for confirmation.

t.a: When should I refer for surgery?
t.b: When imaging shows obstruction, perforation, or a suspicious mass.

whenToSeekHelp: Acute abdominal pain with rapid girth increase
